NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetson-ai-lab:
This repository provides tutorials and resources for generative AI on NVIDIA Jetson.
It provides optimized deployment containers, model scripts, and performance benchmarks.
It helps developers deploy generative models directly on edge hardware.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge devices.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/synthetic_data_generation_:
This workflow generates synthetic training data for computer vision models.
It uses Omniverse Replicator with domain randomization to export KITTI annotations.
It reduces the need for manual dataset collection and labeling.
It operates in NVIDIA Isaac Sim on local GPUs or cloud instances.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/nanosam:
This library is a distilled Segment Anything model for real-time segmentation.
It executes an optimized MobileSAM image encoder using NVIDIA TensorRT.
It provides low-latency image mask generation with minimal memory overhead.
It operates locally on NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge devices.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/nanoowl:
This project optimizes open-world object detection for real-time inference.
It accelerates OWL-ViT and CLIP vision-language models using TensorRT.
It enables fast open-vocabulary detection without model retraining.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge devices.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/deepstream_libraries:
This package provides Python bindings for GPU-accelerated multimedia and computer vision.
It integrates CVCUDA, NvImageCodec, and PyNvVideoCodec into unified Python APIs.
It simplifies hardware-accelerated video decoding and tensor preprocessing.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson devices and Linux GPU workstations.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/whisper_trt:
This project optimizes OpenAI Whisper for real-time automatic speech recognition.
It compiles Whisper transformer models into TensorRT execution engines.
It speeds up speech transcription while reducing GPU memory usage.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin modules and desktop GPUs.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetson-platform-services:
This software collection provides modular AI microservices for edge application development.
It orchestrates containerized services for video analytics and vision-language alerts.
It simplifies deployment and scaling of edge vision pipelines.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin devices running JetPack.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetson-copilot:
This reference application provides a local conversational AI assistant.
It combines local large language models with retrieval-augmented generation.
It processes private documents locally without sending data to external clouds.
It operates directly on NVIDIA Jetson Orin edge devices.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/ros2_nanollm:
This package provides ROS 2 nodes for language and vision-language models.
It runs NanoLLM inference to generate real-time scene descriptions from camera topics.
It integrates multimodal language capabilities directly into robot navigation stacks.
It operates on NVIDIA Jetson Orin platforms on mobile robots.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/DeepStream_Coding_Agent:
This toolkit provides structured AI prompts and skills for video pipeline development.
It guides AI coding assistants to write valid NVIDIA DeepStream applications.
It accelerates application development and reduces configuration errors.
It operates in developer coding environments such as Cursor and Claude Code.
NVIDIA-AI-IOT/jetson-device-skills:
This catalog contains automated diagnostic and management skills for edge hardware.
It runs diagnostic scripts and audits memory, runtimes, and model serving.
It assists autonomous agents in managing system resources on booted devices.
It operates locally on live NVIDIA Jetson devices.
isaac-sim/IsaacGymEnvs:
This repository provides reinforcement learning benchmark environments for robotics.
It simulates thousands of robots in parallel using Isaac Gym GPU physics.
It speeds up policy training by eliminating CPU-to-GPU data transfers.
It operates on NVIDIA workstation GPUs.
isaac-sim/OmniIsaacGymEnvs:
This framework provides reinforcement learning environments inside Omniverse Isaac Sim.
It runs GPU-accelerated PhysX simulation and multi-camera rendering in parallel.
It trains complex locomotion and manipulation policies using photo-realistic simulation.
It operates within NVIDIA Isaac Sim on RTX-enabled workstations.
isaac-sim/IsaacLab:
This unified open-source framework trains robot learning policies.
It combines GPU-accelerated physics, actuator models, and reinforcement learning libraries.
It simplifies research across legged locomotion and robotic manipulation tasks.
It operates inside NVIDIA Isaac Sim on workstation and cloud GPUs.
isaac-sim/IsaacSim-ros_workspaces:
This repository provides pre-configured ROS and ROS 2 workspaces for simulation.
It packages ROS 2 Humble and Jazzy packages that communicate with simulation topics.
It provides ready-to-build bridge packages between ROS nodes and simulated robots.
It operates on Linux workstations connecting to NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
isaac-sim/urdf-importer-extension:
This extension converts Unified Robot Description Format files into USD assets.
It parses URDF kinematic trees and generates physics-ready USD robot definitions.
It imports standard ROS robot models directly into the simulation engine.
It operates as an extension inside NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
isaac-sim/mjcf-importer-extension:
This extension imports MuJoCo XML robot model files into Universal Scene Description.
It parses MJCF kinematic bodies, joints, and collision geometries into USD.
It allows MuJoCo benchmark models to run inside Omniverse physics environments.
It operates as an Omniverse extension inside NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
isaac-sim/IsaacAutomator:
This automation tool deploys remote Isaac Sim workstations to cloud providers.
It executes automated provisioning scripts across AWS, GCP, and Azure.
It creates ready-to-use cloud simulation instances without manual system setup.
It operates on public cloud GPU virtual machines.
isaac-sim/IsaacLabExtensionTemplate:
This project template provides a starting structure for Isaac Lab extensions.
It defines directory layouts, configuration files, and testing boilerplate.
It standardizes custom reinforcement learning environment development for users.
It operates within the Isaac Lab simulation ecosystem on workstations.
isaac-sim/IsaacSimZMQ:
This extension provides a ZeroMQ network bridge for NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
It streams simulation data and receives control commands using Protobuf messages.
It enables bidirectional communication between simulator scenes and external programs.
It operates inside NVIDIA Isaac Sim on desktop workstations.
isaac-sim/isaacsim-app-template:
This project template scaffolds standalone Kit applications based on Isaac Sim.
It configures Omniverse Kit SDK feature branches, dependencies, and build scripts.
It accelerates the creation of custom robotics simulation applications.

isaac-sim/isaac-xr-teleop-sample-client-:
This application enables immersive robot teleoperation using spatial computing headsets.
It streams stereo video and spatial pose data via CloudXR.
It lets operators control simulated robots with natural hand tracking.
It operates on Apple Vision Pro connecting to NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
isaac-sim/IsaacLabTutorial:
This tutorial repository teaches developers how to build robot learning tasks.
It provides progressive step-by-step code branches for Isaac Lab workflows.
It helps researchers learn environment creation and policy training quickly.
It operates in Isaac Lab environments on Linux GPU workstations.
isaac-sim/IsaacLabEvalTasks:
This benchmark suite evaluates humanoid manipulation policies in simulation.
It simulates closed-loop industrial tasks such as nut pouring and pipe sorting.
It measures the accuracy and success rates of GR00T humanoid policies.
It operates within Isaac Lab on GPU workstations.
isaac-sim/IsaacSim:
This robotics simulation platform generates virtual worlds for autonomous robots.
It computes rigid body dynamics and ray-traced sensor data using NVIDIA Omniverse.
It trains and validates robot perception and control before physical deployment.
It operates on workstation GPUs and cloud instances.
isaac-sim/isaac-launchable:
This launcher provides browser-based access to pre-configured Isaac Sim environments.
It streams interactive simulation interfaces and remote VS Code sessions via Brev.
It removes local installation requirements for robotics developers.
It operates in cloud containers accessible through standard web browsers.
isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena:
This simulation framework constructs modular multi-robot evaluation environments.
It composes robotic embodiments, interactive objects, and procedural scenes.
It tests policy generalization across diverse multi-agent robotic tasks.
It operates inside NVIDIA Isaac Lab on GPU workstations.
isaac-sim/isaac-teleop-device-plugins:
This plugin collection connects hardware tracking devices to simulation teleoperation.
It links Manus hand-tracking gloves and controllers to Isaac Sim APIs.
It captures real human motions to drive simulated robotic hands.
It operates on Linux workstations running NVIDIA Isaac Sim.
isaac-sim/Sim-to-Real-SO-101-Workshop:
This workshop repository demonstrates physical AI sim-to-real transfer workflows.
It trains control policies in Isaac Lab and deploys them to SO-101 robot arms.
It verifies that simulated manipulation behaviors transfer to physical hardware.
It operates across Isaac Lab workstations and physical robot arms.
NVlabs/geomapnet:
This software performs camera localization using visual geometry and deep neural networks.
It predicts camera poses from image sequences using map consistency loss functions.
It improves visual localization accuracy without manual feature matching.
It operates on Linux workstations running PyTorch.
NVlabs/learningrigidity:
This vision system estimates 3D motion fields in dynamic camera scenes.
It decomposes optical flow into rigid camera motion and non-rigid object movement.
It improves 3D scene reconstruction when objects move independently.
It operates on desktop GPUs processing dynamic video sequences.
NVlabs/Deep_Object_Pose:
This neural network detects known 3D objects and estimates their 6-DoF poses.
It detects object keypoints from single RGB images and computes poses via PnP.
It provides accurate object poses for robot manipulation without depth sensors.
It operates on robot companion computers and GPU workstations via ROS.
NVlabs/FLAT:
This dataset and processing library removes artifacts from Time-of-Flight depth cameras.
It simulates raw sensor measurements and applies deep networks to correct noise.
It removes multi-path interference and motion blur to improve depth accuracy.
It operates on GPU research workstations processing depth sensor data.
NVlabs/6dof-graspnet:
This model generates diverse 6-DoF grasp candidates for robotic manipulators.
It samples grasp poses using a variational autoencoder conditioned on 3D point clouds.
It generates successful grasp orientations for unseen objects in cluttered scenes.
It operates on GPU workstations controlling robot arm grippers.
NVlabs/wetectron:
This computer vision system trains object detection models from weak annotations.
It learns bounding boxes using only image-level tags, points, or scribbles.
It lowers dataset annotation costs for computer vision training.
It operates on Linux GPU workstations running PyTorch.
NVlabs/DREAM:
This system estimates camera-to-robot extrinsic calibration from single RGB images.
It detects robot joint keypoints with neural networks and solves forward kinematics.
It eliminates manual calibration targets like checkerboards.
It operates on robotic manipulator arms with external or eye-in-hand cameras.
NVlabs/latentfusion:
This neural system reconstructs 3D shapes and estimates 6D poses of unseen objects.
It renders latent neural representations and optimizes alignment against input views.
It estimates poses of novel objects without requiring exact 3D CAD models.
It operates on GPU workstations running PyTorch.
NVlabs/acronym:
This dataset and toolset provides large-scale robotic grasp annotations.
It evaluates millions of parallel-jaw grasps on 3D meshes using NVIDIA FleX physics.
It supplies labeled training data for deep learning grasp models.
It operates on data processing workstations and simulation servers.
NVlabs/DefGraspSim:
This simulation framework tests robotic grasping performance on deformable objects.
It simulates soft body deformations and contact mechanics during grasp trials.
It evaluates grasp stability on flexible materials before physical tests.
It operates in physics simulators on Linux GPU workstations.
NVlabs/contact_graspnet:
This neural network predicts 6-DoF grasp poses directly from 3D point clouds.
It identifies grasp contact point candidates using deep feature representations.
It generates stable grasps in cluttered scenes without object mesh models.
It operates on GPU systems controlling robotic manipulator arms.
NVlabs/storm:
This toolkit computes reactive robot motions using GPU-accelerated optimization.
It evaluates trajectory costs in parallel using Model Predictive Path Integral control.
It generates smooth, collision-free robot trajectories in dynamic environments.
It operates on workstation GPUs controlling physical or simulated robot arms.
NVlabs/DIODE:
This algorithm performs data-free knowledge distillation for object detection models.
It inverts trained teacher networks to synthesize images for student model training.
It transfers model knowledge without requiring original private training datasets.
It operates on Linux GPU workstations running PyTorch.
NVlabs/AL-MDN:
This active learning system selects informative training images for object detectors.
It quantifies localization and classification uncertainties using mixture density networks.
It reduces human labeling effort by requesting labels only for difficult samples.
It operates on GPU training servers for computer vision pipelines.
NVlabs/oscar:
This control framework trains adaptive manipulation policies for robot arms.
It combines operational space control with reinforcement learning in Isaac Gym.
It produces compliant, robust manipulation behaviors under varying physical dynamics.
It operates within NVIDIA Isaac Gym on GPU workstations.
NVlabs/CenterPose:
This network estimates category-level 6-DoF object poses from single RGB images.
It detects 3D bounding box keypoints and CAD-less object shapes in a single stage.
It identifies poses of novel object instances within known categories in real time.
It operates on GPU workstations and robotic vision systems.
NVlabs/GLAMR:
This vision system recovers global 3D human motion from dynamic camera videos.
It estimates human body meshes and camera trajectories while handling occlusions.
It reconstructs accurate human kinematics without static motion capture rigs.
It operates on GPU workstations analyzing single-view video sequences.
NVlabs/ACID:
This framework learns visual dynamics models for deformable object manipulation.
It predicts action-conditioned point cloud dynamics using implicit neural representations.
It plans manipulation trajectories for flexible objects like cloth and ropes.
It operates on GPU workstations guiding robotic manipulation arms.
NVlabs/handover-sim:
This benchmark environment simulates human-to-robot object handover interactions.
It replays human grasp trajectories and evaluates robot receiving policies in PyBullet.
It provides standardized metrics to measure robot handover success.
It operates in simulation environments on Linux workstations.
NVlabs/DiffRL:
This reinforcement learning algorithm trains control policies using differentiable physics.
It computes analytic policy gradients through parallel GPU simulation with SHAC.
It achieves faster sample efficiency than derivative-free reinforcement learning.
It operates on workstation GPUs running parallel physics simulations.
NVlabs/RVT:
This visual manipulation model predicts precise 3D end-effector actions.
It re-projects multi-view scene features into virtual camera perspectives using transformers.
It learns millimeter-accurate manipulation tasks from few demonstration examples.
It operates on GPU workstations controlling robotic arm manipulators.
NVlabs/diff-dope:
This algorithm refines 6-DoF object poses using differentiable rendering.
It minimizes reprojection errors across RGB, depth, and edge channels via gradient descent.
It corrects initial pose estimation errors to achieve high geometric precision.
It operates on GPU workstations supporting robotic perception pipelines.
NVlabs/curobo:
This CUDA library computes collision-free robot kinematics and motion plans.
It executes parallel inverse kinematics and trajectory optimization on the GPU.
It generates safe robot trajectories within milliseconds for real-time control.
It operates on NVIDIA GPUs driving robotic manipulator arms.
NVlabs/handover-sim2real:
This system trains human-to-robot handover policies for real-world execution.
It predicts robot receiving motions from segmented depth point clouds.
It transfers simulated handover policies directly to physical robots without fine-tuning.
It operates on robot arm workstations equipped with depth cameras.
NVlabs/FoundationPose:
This foundation model performs 6D pose estimation and tracking for novel objects.
It computes poses using neural rendering and contrastive feature matching.
It tracks unseen objects accurately without object-specific training or fine-tuning.
It operates on GPU workstations and autonomous robotic perception platforms.
NVlabs/3DGM:
This framework reconstructs 3D Gaussian splatting maps with 2D semantic segmentations.
It optimizes 3D Gaussians using self-supervised features across multiple scene traversals.
It builds clean 3D maps and separates static structures from transient objects.
It operates on GPU workstations processing mobile mapping sensor logs.
NVlabs/Eagle:
This vision-language model family performs high-resolution visual reasoning and perception.
It combines multi-resolution vision encoders with large language model backbones.
It processes fine-grained visual details and localizes image elements accurately.
It operates on GPU servers and cloud inference instances.
NVlabs/DRAIL:
This imitation learning algorithm trains robotic policies from suboptimal demonstrations.
It optimizes reward functions using diffusion models within adversarial learning loops.
It improves policy performance even when expert demonstrations contain errors.
It operates on GPU training clusters for robotic control policies.
NVlabs/IsaacLabEureka:
This automation framework designs reinforcement learning reward functions for robots.
It prompts large language models to write and iterate reward code in Isaac Lab.
It automates complex reward engineering for robotic skill acquisition.
It operates on workstation GPUs connected to LLM APIs.
NVlabs/object_centric_diffusion:
This imitation learning framework generates manipulation trajectories via diffusion.
It predicts SE(3) object trajectories rather than raw joint commands.
It generalizes manipulation skills across varying robot kinematics and camera positions.
It operates on GPU workstations controlling robot arm manipulators.
NVlabs/ProtoMotions:
This simulation framework trains motor control policies for humanoid robots.
It runs GPU-parallel physics and reinforcement learning algorithms.
It accelerates the synthesis of human-like locomotion and agile whole-body behaviors.
It operates on workstation GPUs running Isaac Sim or Isaac Gym.
NVlabs/scene_synthesizer:
This Python package proceduralizes 3D scene generation for robot manipulation.

NVlabs/AHA:

NVlabs/vla0:
